title: A finite conjugation jet detects the scheme-theoretic centre
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $F$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $e\in G(F)$ be its identity, let $B=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ be its coordinate algebra, and let $I=\ker(e^*:B\to F)$ be the augmentation ideal. For each integer $r\geq1$, put $V_r=B/I^{r+1}$ and $J_r^i=\operatorname{im}(I^i\to V_r)$ for $0\leq i\leq r+1$. The vector space $V_r$ is finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Pullback by inverse conjugation defines a homomorphism of group schemes $\rho_r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V_r)$, where $\operatorname{GL}(V_r)(A)$ is the group of invertible $A$-linear maps of $A\otimes_F V_r$. Explicitly, for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, $\rho_{r,A}(g)$ is pullback on functions on the closed subscheme of $G_A$ defined by $(A\otimes_F I)^{r+1}$ under $x\mapsto g^{-1}xg$. It preserves every $A\otimes_F J_r^i$, acts by $A$-algebra automorphisms, and acts identically on $A\otimes_F(V_r/J_r^1)=A$. The maps $V_{r+1}\to V_r$ are equivariant. There is an integer $r_0\geq1$ such that for every $r\geq r_0$ the scheme-theoretic kernel of $\rho_r$ is $Z(G)$, the closed subgroup scheme of [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. Equivalently, for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, $\rho_{r,A}(g)=1$ if and only if $g\in Z(G)(A)$. Quotients and ideal powers have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and affine coordinates and representations use [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-wf-algebraic-representations].

source.place: Corollary 8.10 and proof of Proposition 8.9, printed p.150. The coordinate quotient B/I^(r+1) is canonically the local quotient O_e/m_e^(r+1): elements outside I are invertible modulo I^(r+1). Inverse conjugation is the left-action convention on functions.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $B$ is a finitely generated $F$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], it is Noetherian: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,F$. Choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$, and put $t_j=b_j-e^*(b_j)$. The $t_j$ still generate $B$ as an $F$-algebra and generate $I$ as an ideal: any polynomial in them with zero constant term belongs to $(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$. Thus the images of monomials $t_1^{a_1}\cdots t_d^{a_d}$ of total degree at most $r$ span $V_r$, proving finite-dimensionality. For any $F$-algebra $A$, the canonical map $(A\otimes_F B)/(A\otimes_F I^{r+1})\to A\otimes_F V_r$ is an isomorphism. Indeed, choose a basis of $I^{r+1}$ and extend it to a basis of $B$; tensoring gives direct sums of copies of $A$, and the quotient deletes precisely the first basis vectors. Multiplication of pure tensors gives $(A\otimes_F I)^{r+1}=A\otimes_F I^{r+1}$. These identifications also apply to each $I^i$ and to the truncation maps.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, finite local quotients and base extension; explicit affine monomial and basis verification. Stacks 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: For $g\in G(A)$ write $c_g(x)=gxg^{-1}$. The group laws make $c_{g^{-1}}$ an $A$-scheme automorphism of $G_A$ fixing its identity section. Consequently its pullback $T_g$ is an $A$-algebra automorphism of $A\otimes_F B$ preserving the kernel $A\otimes_F I$ of evaluation at that section, hence all its powers. It descends to an invertible $A$-linear map on $A\otimes_F V_r$. This construction is natural in $A$ because multiplication, inverse, and identity are scheme morphisms. Since $c_{(gh)^{-1}}=c_{h^{-1}}\circ c_{g^{-1}}$, contravariance gives $T_{gh}=T_gT_h$; $T_1=1$. Thus these maps are natural group homomorphisms. The finite-dimensional clause of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] gives the group-scheme homomorphism $\rho_r:G\to\operatorname{GL}(V_r)$ with exactly these algebra-point values.

source.place: Proposition 8.9 and Corollary 8.10, printed p.150; Chapter 4(a), printed pp.83--84. Inverse conjugation checks the left representation convention.

proof.text: The preservation of $(A\otimes_F I)^i$ just proved gives preservation of $A\otimes_F J_r^i$. Each $T_g$ preserves products and $1$, and its induced action modulo $A\otimes_F I$ is the identity because it fixes the identity section and is an $A$-algebra map. Finally $T_g$ on $A\otimes_F B$ preserves both $I^{r+2}$ and $I^{r+1}$ after scalar extension, so the two quotient maps satisfy $q_{r+1,r}T_g=T_gq_{r+1,r}$ on the class of every $b\in B$. These classes generate after scalar extension, proving equivariance of $V_{r+1}\to V_r$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, descending sequence of jet kernels; the filtration and equivariance are the quotient calculation.

proof.text: Choose an $F$-basis of each $V_r$ and write $a_{ij}^{(r)}\in B$ for the matrix coefficients of the universal action $T_{\mathrm{id}_B}$ on $B\otimes_F V_r$. The dictionary in [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] says that for $g:B\to A$ the matrix entries of $\rho_{r,A}(g)$ are $g(a_{ij}^{(r)})$. Set $L_r=(a_{ij}^{(r)}-\delta_{ij})\subset B$ and $H_r=\operatorname{Spec}(B/L_r)$. The affine and quotient descriptions show that $H_r(A)$ is precisely $\ker\rho_{r,A}$ for every $A$. Thus $H_r$ is the scheme-theoretic kernel (the fibre product over the identity), and is a closed subgroup: each of its algebra-point subsets is a kernel subgroup, as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Equivariance of the surjection $V_{r+1}\to V_r$ implies $H_{r+1}(A)\subseteq H_r(A)$: an identity map on the source induces the identity on the quotient. Applying this with $A=B/L_{r+1}$ and its universal point shows $L_r\subseteq L_{r+1}$, with no replacement by radical ideals.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150: H_n=Ker(rho_n) and its descending sequence. Matrix equations spell out the scheme structures.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-module-acc] to the Noetherian ring $B$ and its cyclic module $M=B$, generated by $1$. The increasing sequence of submodules $L_1\subseteq L_2\subseteq\cdots$ stabilizes. Thus there is $r_0\geq1$ with $L_r=L_{r_0}$ for every $r\geq r_0$, and $H_r=H_{r_0}$ as closed subgroup schemes, including their nilpotents. Put $H=H_{r_0}$. The inclusions for the earlier indices imply $H\subseteq H_r$ for every $r\geq1$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, Noetherian stabilization; Stacks 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic), ascending chain condition for submodules.

proof.text: The identity makes $G$ nonempty. Since $G$ is connected, its identity component is all of $G$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], this component is geometrically irreducible, in particular irreducible over $F$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], smoothness makes the fibre of $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, which is $G$ itself, reduced. Therefore $G$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Since $G$ is affine, $B$ is a domain by that same definition. This is the reducedness needed when passing from local information at $e$ to global functions.

source.place: Corollary 8.10, printed p.150, connected conjugation source. Stacks 0B7R (proposition-connected-component), 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); reducedness is explicit here.

proof.text: The ideal $I$ is maximal since $B/I=F$. Let $R=B_I$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=IR$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with $M=R$ and ideal $\mathfrak m$: the unique maximal ideal is the Jacobson radical and $R$ is generated by $1$ as an $R$-module. Thus $\bigcap_n\mathfrak m^n=0$. If $b\in\bigcap_n I^n$, its image in $R$ belongs to every $\mathfrak m^n$, so it vanishes. The localization map $B\to R$ is injective: vanishing of $b/1$ means $sb=0$ for some $s\notin I$; $s\ne0$ and $B$ is a domain. Hence $b=0$, proving $\bigcap_n I^n=0$ in $B$.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, Krull intersection argument. Stacks 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), part (2).

proof.text: This separation remains valid with arbitrary coefficient algebra $A$: $\bigcap_n(A\otimes_F I^n)=0$ inside $A\otimes_F B$. To check it, choose an $F$-basis $(u_\lambda)$ of $A$. Express an element as a finite sum $\sum_\lambda u_\lambda\otimes b_\lambda$. Under $A\otimes_F B=\bigoplus_\lambda B$, the subspace $A\otimes_F I^n$ is $\bigoplus_\lambda I^n$. Membership for every $n$ forces each of its finitely many coefficients into $\bigcap_n I^n=0$. This uses neither finite generation nor reducedness of $A$. Omitting the finitely many exponents $0,1$ does not change the intersection.

source.place: Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, base extension of local quotients and Krull intersection; explicit coefficient calculation for arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, test algebras.

proof.text: Fix any $F$-algebra $A$ and $g\in H(A)$. Since $H\subseteq H_r$ for every $r$, the difference $T_g(b)-1\otimes b$ lies in $A\otimes_F I^{r+1}$ for every $r\geq1$ and $b\in B$. Step 8 gives $T_g(b)=1\otimes b$; $A$-linearity gives $T_g=1$ on $A\otimes_F B$. The affine correspondence makes $c_{g^{-1}}$ the identity morphism of $G_A$. After any $A$-algebra extension $A'$, it is still the identity, so $g_{A'}^{-1}xg_{A'}=x$ for every $x\in G(A')$. By the universal centre description in [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change], this says $g\in Z(G)(A)$. Conversely, a central $g$ has identity conjugation on $G_A$: apply the universal commutation condition to the universal point over $A\otimes_F B$. Its pullback, and therefore each jet action, is the identity. Thus $H(A)=Z(G)(A)$ for every $A$. These are equal closed subgroup schemes: if their defining ideals are $L,J\subset B$, the universal points over $B/L$ and $B/J$ give $J\subseteq L$ and $L\subseteq J$. Combining with Step 5 proves $\ker\rho_r=Z(G)$ for every $r\geq r_0$ and the stated equivalence on all algebra points.

source.place: Corollary 8.10 and proof of Proposition 8.9, printed pp.150--151; scheme-theoretic centre as in Proposition 1.92, printed pp.33--34. Universal points replace a check on field-valued points alone.

proof_origin.place: Corollary 8.10 and Proposition 8.9, printed pp.150--151, expanded in affine coordinates with Noetherian ideals and a coefficientwise Krull-intersection calculation.

tool_uses.why: The affine coordinate algebra of G is finite type over F; this is a generic affine-scheme tool, not a replacement for the unit route.
Hilbert basis theorem gives Noetherianity of B from its finite generation over the field.
Ascending chains of ideals of B stabilize scheme structures, not only supports.
Smoothness over the field gives reducedness of G; the group component theorem supplies irreducibility.
Localizing B at the augmentation maximal ideal preserves Noetherianity.
Krull intersection applied to the local ring B_I gives separation at the identity.
